question: According to the WHO ICD-11 (2018) classification, which of the following visual acuities (best-corrected, better eye) defines BLINDNESS?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 6/60 is the threshold for 'moderate visual impairment' in some older classifications, but not WHO ICD-11 blindness. Blindness requires a more severe threshold.

answers.text: Worse than 3/60 (or visual field <10 degrees) in the better eye

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. WHO ICD-11 defines blindness as best-corrected visual acuity worse than 3/60 (or less than 10 degrees of visual field around central fixation) in the better eye. Category 3 = severe visual impairment (3/60–1/60), Category 4 = profound (1/60–light perception), Category 5 = no light perception.

1/60 is the threshold between severe and profound visual impairment in WHO ICD-11 — both are within the blindness spectrum, but blindness begins at worse than 3/60. This answer understates the threshold.
6/18 is the threshold for mild visual impairment (or the cut-off for driving standards in some jurisdictions). It is far from the blindness threshold.

overallFeedback.feedback: WHO ICD-11 blindness = VA worse than 3/60 OR visual field < 10 degrees around central fixation in the better eye (best corrected). India's NPCBVI programme historically used <6/60 with correction, but the international standard is 3/60.
Correct. WHO ICD-11 blindness: VA worse than 3/60 OR visual field <10°, better eye, best corrected. Memorise both criteria.
